title: The unauthorized regimental band and running a barrack of forty
summary: He was attached to the band by the Colonel's grace, ended up second in charge as a Technician 5th Grade, and ran the barrack of a marching band.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: The Army band, you're speaking of.

Well, I'll tell you, the Army band, the Army had authorized bands which consisted of 28 pieces and a director who was an officer, an officer. He wasn't a Lieutenant. He was just a step below a Lieutenant. Funny how these things escape you. Well, anyway, so we were all attached. When you came into the regiment, by the good grace of the Colonel, if you were drafted as just a soldier and you were put in a company, like whatever company, you were Company M, Company L, Company K, and you made it known that you were a musician, you were allowed by the Colonel to become attached to the band. He didn't make you a soldier, see? So I was attached to the band. I was a member of Headquarters Company. I was in Headquarters Company, attached to the band. I was always attached to something. I never was a full member of anything while I was in the Army.
So that band -- so when we were shipped out, the band, authorized band, wasn't under the jurisdiction of the regiment. So when the band was shipped out the Colonel took
all the musicians who were attached to the band with him, down to Breckenridge. Then he gave us the barrack to form another band. So that's how that came about.

Then Breckenridge. So -- well, incidentally, when I -- so, you see, it was unauthorized, so we didn't have the TO. The TO is the Table of Organization which means, you know, you have so many ranks in whatever. So ours wasn't like that. We had a Sergeant who was in charge of the band, then by that time I was a Technician 5th Grade, which is a two-striper, you know, a Corporal.
And I was second in charge of the band, see? So when he went on furlough, I was in charge. A two-striper in charge of a barrack of 40 people, you know. And I ran it. I ran the barrack.
So what kind of band was it? Was it a marching band, or --
Yeah, a marching band, I'm speaking of. Oh, yes, strictly a marching band.
